Waste Management Customer Notifications

Regional Waste Management Provider · Regional (Multi-County) · Waste Management

A regional waste management company used Cornerstone's variable-data printing and multi-county presort capability to deliver zone-specific service-change notifications to thousands of residential customers within a regulatory deadline, each letter customized to that household's exact pickup schedule and rate structure.

Variable-Data Letters

Processing

The Challenge

A regional waste management company needed to notify thousands of residential customers across multiple counties about service schedule changes, rate adjustments, and new recycling program guidelines. The notifications needed to reach every customer household on time, with different versions for different service zones, and comply with regulatory notification requirements.

Our Solution

Cornerstone handled the variable-data printing, producing customized letters for each service zone with zone-specific schedules and rate information. We processed the company's customer database through CASS/DPV validation and NCOA move-update to ensure maximum deliverability, then presorted the mailing for optimal postage rates across multiple ZIP codes and counties.

The Results

All notifications were delivered within the required notification window. The variable-data approach ensured each customer received accurate, zone-specific information rather than a generic notice. The waste management company has since used Cornerstone for all customer communications, including annual rate notices, service change alerts, and recycling education materials.

Background

Waste management and utility companies face a unique direct mail challenge: their mailings are not marketing — they are operational communications that customers are legally required to receive. Service schedule changes, rate adjustments, and recycling program modifications must be communicated to every affected household within specific timeframes, often mandated by state or municipal regulations. This regional waste management provider serves residential customers across multiple counties in the Hudson Valley region, with different service zones following different pickup schedules, rate structures, and recycling guidelines. A one-size-fits-all notification letter would create confusion — each customer needed to receive information specific to their service zone. The company's previous approach of manually printing and mailing zone-specific letters was labor-intensive, error-prone, and could not scale as their service territory expanded.

Strategy & Execution

Variable-Data Printing

The core of this project was variable-data printing (VDP) — producing customized letters where specific content blocks changed based on each customer's service zone. Zone-specific elements included: pickup day schedules, rate tables, recycling sorting instructions, and customer service contact numbers. The master template remained consistent (company branding, general messaging, legal language), while variable blocks were populated from the customer database during the print run.

Database Processing and Address Validation

The company's customer database required thorough cleaning before mailing. We processed the file through CASS/DPV (Coding Accuracy Support System / Delivery Point Validation) to verify that every address was a valid, deliverable USPS address. NCOA (National Change of Address) processing identified customers who had moved, and we flagged these records for the company's billing department. Duplicate detection eliminated cases where customers appeared multiple times in the database.

Multi-Zone Presort Optimization

Because the mailing spanned multiple counties and ZIP codes with zone-specific content, the presort had to be coordinated carefully. Our software sorted the variable-data output into optimal postal presort groupings while maintaining the zone-specific content integrity — ensuring that each customer received the correct version of the letter regardless of how the postal sort organized the mail stream.

Regulatory Compliance Documentation

The company required proof of mailing for regulatory compliance — evidence that all affected customers were notified within the required timeframe. We provided a detailed mailing report including piece counts by zone, mailing dates, USPS acceptance receipts, and address validation summaries. This documentation serves as the company's regulatory record in the event of any compliance inquiry.

Design Approach

Utility notification letters prioritize clarity over marketing aesthetics. The design used a clean, structured layout with clearly delineated sections: the schedule change summary at the top (what changed), the new schedule details in the middle (what to do), and customer service contact information at the bottom (who to call with questions). Rate tables were formatted as simple, easy-to-read grids. Recycling instructions used icon-based visual guides (what goes in which bin) that work for recipients with limited English proficiency. The company's logo and branding appeared in the header, but the overall tone was informational rather than promotional.

Postal Strategy

Customer notification mailings were sent via USPS First-Class Mail for two critical reasons: First-Class Mail is forwarded to the customer's new address if they have moved (Marketing Mail is not), and First-Class provides return service for undeliverable addresses. Both features are essential for utility notifications — if a customer has moved, the notification needs to follow them to their new address, and undeliverable returns alert the company that a customer may have left their service area. The presort processing across multiple counties achieved significant First-Class postal discounts compared to single-piece rates.

Key Takeaways

Variable-data printing transforms what would be a manual, zone-by-zone printing process into a single automated production run. The company previously printed separate letter versions for each zone and manually sorted them — a process that took days and was prone to errors. VDP reduced the production time to hours and eliminated the risk of customers receiving the wrong zone's information.

Address validation on customer databases catches more issues than most companies expect. The initial CASS/DPV processing on this account identified a significant percentage of addresses with deliverability issues — apartment numbers missing, ZIP codes incorrect, streets misspelled. Cleaning these records improved deliverability and also helped the company maintain a more accurate billing database.

Regulatory documentation requirements make professional mailing services essential for utility companies. A mailing report from a USPS-certified presort provider carries more weight in regulatory proceedings than internal records of hand-delivered or self-mailed notices.

The ongoing relationship has expanded beyond notifications to include customer education materials (recycling guides, contamination reduction mailers) and new customer welcome packets — all leveraging the variable-data infrastructure we built for the notification mailings.

Industry Context

Utility and municipal service notifications represent a steady, recurring segment of the direct mail industry. Unlike marketing campaigns that fluctuate with budgets and seasons, regulatory notifications must go out — they are not optional. Waste management companies, water utilities, electric cooperatives, and municipal governments all share the need for accurate, timely, zone-specific customer communications. Cornerstone's variable-data printing and presort mailing capabilities make us a natural partner for these organizations, particularly in the multi-county Hudson Valley region where service zones cross municipal and county boundaries.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is variable-data printing?
Variable-data printing (VDP) produces customized documents in a single print run — each piece can have different text, images, or data pulled from a database. For utility notifications, this means each customer receives a letter with their specific service zone schedule, rates, and instructions, all printed in one continuous production run rather than printing separate versions for each zone.

How does CASS/DPV address validation work?
CASS (Coding Accuracy Support System) and DPV (Delivery Point Validation) are USPS address quality programs. CASS standardizes addresses to USPS formatting standards, while DPV verifies that each address is an actual, active delivery point. Together, they ensure your mailing reaches valid addresses and qualifies for presort postal discounts. Processing your customer database through CASS/DPV before mailing typically improves deliverability and reduces waste.

Can Cornerstone provide proof of mailing for regulatory compliance?
Cornerstone provides detailed mailing reports including piece counts, mailing dates, USPS acceptance receipts, and address validation summaries. For clients with regulatory notification requirements, this documentation serves as an official record that all affected parties were notified within the required timeframe.

How often do utility companies typically mail customer notifications?
Most utility companies require 2-4 major notification mailings per year: annual rate adjustment notices, schedule changes (seasonal or permanent), new service introductions (recycling program changes, composting programs), and regulatory compliance notifications. Many also send periodic customer education materials. Cornerstone maintains the data infrastructure so each mailing builds on the previous one's database work.
